$comment: Capability vocabulary for the native bridge between a SIROS web-view wrapper app and the page it hosts. Single source of truth: tools/gen_bridge_capabilities.py generates the Kotlin, Swift and TypeScript from this file; CI fails if they drift. Mirrors the Wallet Messaging Protocol's capability map (WmpProfile.capabilities / WmpRegistry.allCapabilities): a descriptor is a map from capability id to that capability's parameters, and a capability that is absent is not offered. Ids are stable once published; retire with `deprecated`, never rename.

descriptor.$comment: What a host advertises to the page. `bridge` is the descriptor schema itself; `vocabulary` says which version of this file the ids come from, so a page can tell 'unknown id' from 'older host'.

vocabulary.description: The vocabulary_version this host was built against.

name.description: Host application id (Android applicationId / iOS bundle id).

sdk_version.description: SIROS SDK version the host links.

capabilities.description: Capability id to its parameters object. Present means offered.
Native WebAuthn create()/get() in place of the WebView's, so security keys reach the page over the SDK's own CTAP2 transports and platform passkeys carry the PRF extension.

prf.description: Assertions can return the WebAuthn PRF extension output.

security_key_transports.description: CTAP2 transports available to the page: `usb`, `nfc`, `ble`, `hybrid`.

capabilities.description: The host is a W3C Digital Credentials API provider on this device and mirrors the page's credential list into the platform registry; presentation responses are returned through the host.

matcher_version.description: Version of the siros-dc-matcher the host registers.

capabilities.description: Physical identity document scanning and face match, started from the page and returned as an identity-verification result.

provider.description: Vendor of the capture SDK, e.g. `facetec`.

capabilities.description: Host-mediated OpenID Connect login: the authorization request opens in a system browser tab and the response is handed back to the page.

capabilities.deprecated: Superseded by proximity.session; removed once every shipped wrapper advertises the session capability.
capabilities.description: Raw Bluetooth LE byte pipe (client and server) with the ISO 18013-5 session layer implemented by the page.

ISO 18013-5 proximity presentation run natively as a session: device engagement, transport, session encryption and reader authentication in the host; the page supplies credentials, consent and device signatures through callbacks.

nfc_static_handover.description: NFC static handover to BLE is available.

reader_auth.description: Reader authentication against the configured trust lists is evaluated natively.

capabilities.description: Zero-knowledge presentation proofs generated natively. The page decides a proof is needed and supplies credential bytes and transcript; the host resolves the circuit, proves, and calls back for the witness signature.

systems.description: Proof system ids the host can prove for, e.g. `longfellow-libzk-v1`, `vega-mdoc-v1`. From the SDK's ZkMdocPresentation.systemIds().

circuit_cache.description: Circuits are cached on disk across launches.

capabilities.description: Key operations performed natively on a container the page imports and exports around each session: generate, sign, attest, over the SDK's key manager and its WSCD plugins.
Credential matching (DCQL) and presentation assembly performed natively over the imported container.
Authentication and PRF-derived container ownership held natively; the page no longer derives the unwrap key.
A native Wallet Messaging Protocol engine. Reserved so that, if it ever exists, it is one more advertised capability rather than a new detection mechanism.

wmp_capabilities.description: WMP capability names, as WmpRegistry.allCapabilities() reports them: `oid4vci`, `oid4vp`, ...
